milestones.outcome: The pinned allocator runs process-wide in the selected BPR desktop, CLI, update helper and other helpers on native macOS with observable ownership and safe cross-module release.
exit_criteria: Pinned and offline configure controls reject substitute source and distribution refuses the baseline switch.
Apple Silicon and Intel native probes demonstrate allocation/free ownership in selected product executables and a signed installed candidate.
milestones.boundary: A usable macOS product graph and explicit, testable allocator selection; other native platforms retain their own obligations.

milestones.outcome: Native Windows 11 x64 desktop and selected helpers or CLI use one coherent mimalloc override with the actual CRT and packaged DLLs.
exit_criteria: Installed native Windows probes show C, C++, Qt/loaded-library interception and safe cross-module release through startup and shutdown.
milestones.boundary: The Windows process-wide product path, without claiming complete release qualification.

milestones.outcome: Ubuntu 26.04 x64 desktop and selected helpers or CLI use mimalloc on the selected WSL2/WSLg station without injecting it into external child programs.
exit_criteria: Installed Ubuntu 26.04 WSL2/WSLg probes show C, C++, Qt/loaded-library interception, safe cross-module release and a clean child environment.
milestones.boundary: The Linux process-wide product path, without claiming complete release qualification.

milestones.outcome: All selected installers and CLI artifacts carry the verified allocator and matching source/legal inventory, with same-workload performance and memory results.
exit_criteria: Installed runtime closure, notices, SPDX and separate corresponding-source asset agree on the pin; negative package checks reject omissions or extras.
Composed and sanitizer/fuzzer paths pass their focused checks, and matched Release comparisons plus the unchanged memory course report outcomes and pre-existing failures.
milestones.boundary: A distributable candidate and truthful performance record, with no publication or unrelated release/security acceptance.

milestones.outcome: The RFC has criterion-linked evidence, current documentation and explicit native and release limits.
exit_criteria: AC01–AC09 are reconciled to direct observations, and documentation and focused integration gates pass.
milestones.boundary: RFC closeout only; release approval remains with the existing release workflow.
